patch:
diff --git a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
index 1267cc2..19fb03c 100644
--- a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
+++ b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
@@ -57,6 +57,20 @@ Rules:
 - true, echo, printf, pwd, directory listings, and display-only reads are not completion checks.
 - Use replan when the current approach is wrong. Use stop only when blocked, unsafe, or impossible.
 - Keep rationale short. State the current fact and why the selected action changes or proves it.
+- Turns are the scarcest resource (about 40 in total). Combine related work into batches of up to
+  four commands (inspect, change, then test in one batch). Do not spend a turn on a single trivial
+  observation. Write complete files in one command rather than editing in many small steps.
+- Before the first change, extract from the ORIGINAL TASK every literal requirement: exact output
+  paths, file names, formats, CLI/API names, ports, and numeric thresholds. Hidden tests check
+  those literals exactly, so reproduce them verbatim. Re-read the task before calling finish.
+- Prefer finishing with a check that runs the deliverable the way an external grader would (fresh
+  process, the exact documented path and invocation, the real input/output format, and edge cases
+  mentioned in the task). A check that only inspects the files you just wrote is too weak.
+- Do not use stop just because an approach failed or a tool is missing. Try alternatives such as
+  installing from a local mirror, writing the tool yourself, or a simpler algorithm. When a
+  long-running or expensive attempt fails, shrink the experiment before retrying.
+- If most turns are spent, deliver the best working partial solution that meets the stated
+  literals and finish rather than starting a large rewrite.
 """.strip()
 
 _REVIEW_RULES = """
